TDs are not the dominant contributors to the dwarf population today but are likely to be an important source of the low-mass galaxy population.
TDs are not a major contributor to the observed dwarf galaxy population in the local Universe, but that a non-zero contribution is likely.
tidal dwarf galaxies are a minor, but significant, component of the galaxy population in the nearby universe, but that they do not account for all the dwarf galaxies we see in nearby clusters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tidal dwarf galaxies are not formed purely by condensation of gas in tidal tails, but also host a significant component drawn from the disk of the parent galaxy.

the tidal dwarf galaxy formation mechanism is not as efficient in producing massive dwarfs in the local Universe as it is at higher redshifts, and that a significant fraction (�40%) of the dwarfs in the field are not tidal dwarfs.
the TDs have been formed from the gas-rich disk galaxies and they are not likely to be formed from gas-poor disk galaxies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tidal dwarf galaxies are not a one-size-fits-all population.
the majority of TDs are not massive, metal-poor objects that are likely to be dark-matter dominated.
TDs are not a rare phenomenon in nearby galaxies, but rather a common by-product of galaxy mergers.
